recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not rename either element under this old tracker; if FHIR-I wants to soften or constrain the Bundle response comment in light of newer lastUpdated policy, handle that as a new work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-17420 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core Feed change request raised and applied for STU3. It requested documentation that Meta.lastUpdated and Bundle.response.lastModified are semantically equivalent in batch/transaction responses and should generally have the same value, without renaming either element.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git/svn commit 45de2ec6cd07eb9ff714fdfc0619e05d1246da2c, recorded as GF#17420 and svn 14374. That commit added the meta.lastUpdated reference to the then-authoritative Bundle spreadsheet response.lastModified comment and added HTTP Last-Modified equivalence wording to the Meta datatype spreadsheet. Later source refactors migrated the Bundle spreadsheet content into source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml.
additional_context: Bundle is an active infrastructure resource in source/fhir.ini. The current Bundle.entry.response.lastModified comment says the value has to match the same time in the meta header (meta.lastUpdated) when a resource is included. Later issues refine adjacent semantics without reversing this rule: FHIR-20211 documents HTTP Last-Modified's different wire format and is already reconciled on the combined branch; FHIR-45047 clarifies Meta.lastUpdated server-management and out-of-sync scenarios while retaining the read interaction equivalence; FHIR-54516 is only Resolved - change required and outside this default applied/published source-edit scope. Searches found no directly relevant human Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current Bundle StructureDefinition already carries the FHIR-17420 clarification, and the later Meta.lastUpdated guidance does not make the Bundle response note stale because it governs consistency between an included response resource's metadata and its entry response metadata.
